newsitem.title: USA: Georgia indicators signal post-holiday strength.
newsitem.headline: Georgia indicators signal post-holiday strength.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Economic Indicators rose one-tenth of a point in October, signaling that the state's post-holiday economy will remain strong, Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report Wednesday.
Leading indicators rose to 144.46 on a 1988 index base of 100. The index is designed to forecast economic activity three to six months ahead, and has risen for four consecutive months.
"The trend appears to indicate that Georgia's economy will continue to grow at a moderate pace during coming months," Poythress said.

The index of concurrent indicators, which measures present conditions, rose by 1.28 points in October to 144.9 on a 1987 base of 100. It had fallen for the previous two months from an August Olympic high of 147.08.

Leading indicators were nudged upward by increases in the number of new corporate charters and new motor vehicle sales. On the downside, initial jobless claims, residential construction activity and the average length of the manufacturing workweek declined in October.

Titles were issued for 44,298 new motor vechicles during the month, an increase of 2,085 or 4.94 percent over September. Applications for new corporate charters rose to 3,033, an increase of 231 or 8.24 percent over September.
The average length of the manufacturing workweek fell to 42.1 hours in October from 42.5 hours in September.
State revenue collections rose to $895 million in October from $889.8 million in September. That was a gain of 0.62 percent for the month, and 12.07 percent over the year.

State sales tax collections faltered slightly, probably due to the removal on Oct 1 of 2 percent of the state's 4 percent sales tax on groceries. Sales tax collections totaled $351 million in October, down 2.17 percent from September but up 7.91 percent over a year ago.

Nonfarm employment was 3.56 million in October, unchanged from September. The work force is epxected to show big increases in November and December due to the holiday shopping season, and then to fall back in January, Poythress said.
Georgia's unemployment rate was 4.3 percent in October, down from 4.4 percent in September and 4.9 percent a year ago.
Initial jobless claims were 30,139 in October, up 1.56 percent from September but down 13.79 percent from a year ago.
